key_insight: Correcting only teacher-disfavored tokens in incorrect student rollouts improves visual mathematical reasoning without requiring figure descriptions at inference.
engineering_relevance: Training-time perceptual correction can strengthen smaller vision-language models without adding annotation or teacher calls at deployment.
method: Generate on-policy student rollouts for visual math problems.
Use training-only reference descriptions and verified solutions to score incorrect rollouts under a minimal-edit objective, applying corrective loss only to teacher-disfavored tokens.
Apply task-reward reinforcement learning to correct rollouts rather than imitating full teacher responses.
evidence_signal: Across model scales, the method meets or exceeds corresponding base models given reference descriptions at inference, improves low-level geometric perception, and transfers to external math and perception benchmarks.
watch_item: Training requires reference figure descriptions and verified solutions; a frozen same-size teacher remains effective but yields smaller gains than a larger teacher on most metrics.
paper_title: Edit, Don't Imitate: Minimal-Edit On-Policy Distillation for Multimodal Reasoning
